findings.title: Shared upload-file assertion of ContainerRule is never active in any real multipart test
findings.description: SDS wave-8-8 SDS-AC-5 (FR-SVL-006 AC-5) says every container test asserts, through the shared rule, that no upload temporary file of the app is left. ContainerRule.leftovers() only inspects the directory returned by container.uploads(), and that method is called only from ServletRuleTest.java:91. ServletMultipartTest and ServletMultipartDisconnectTest use their own TemporaryFolder (tmp.newFolder("spool")) as tempDirectory, so the rule checks nothing for them. ServletMultipartTest.sdsAc2 (lines 123-142) posts a multipart body and a form and never asserts that the spool dir is empty afterwards, so a leaked spool file in that path is caught by nothing.
findings.suggested_fix: Use container.uploads() instead of TemporaryFolder as the multipart tempDirectory in ServletMultipartTest and ServletMultipartDisconnectTest (keep the explicit empty-dir assertions), so the rule's after() check covers every test that spools uploads.

findings.title: Tight wall-clock upper bounds and fixed sleeps make the SSE/stop tests flaky under load
findings.description: Assertions fail on scheduler noise rather than on a defect: SseDelivery 89 (event within 500 ms of send) and 93 (ping within 1500 ms), ServletStopSseTest.java:147 (stop between 900 and 2000 ms, with a 300 ms sleep at 142 to let buffers fill), ServletStopTest.java:126 (took < 1900) and :142 (<= 2000), ServletStopTest.java:119 (503 within 1000 ms), ServletLifecycleTest.java:135. Several depend on Thread.sleep settling (ServletSseDeliveryTest:85, ServletSseAsyncTest:135 and 237, ServletStopTest:121). A loaded CI host (GC pause, parallel Gradle workers) breaks the 500 ms and deadline+1 s margins without any product bug. ServletStopSseTest.sdsAc3 additionally depends on the OS socket buffers being smaller than the 15 MiB queued; a host with larger autotuned buffers drains it and stop returns early (< 900 ms).
findings.suggested_fix: Keep the contract bounds only where the SDS demands them and widen the margin (or measure the minimum over a few attempts); replace the settle sleeps with condition polls (queue depth / adapter.pool().open()); for the non-reading client, set a small SO_SNDBUF-independent condition (e.g. poll until c.send starts returning false or the queue is above a threshold) instead of a fixed 300 ms sleep.

findings.title: Abort tests drive a hand-copied servlet instead of NaruServeServlet and can NPE on a missing exchange
findings.description: The two abort tests (ServletSseLimitTest 154-185 and ServletSseAsyncTest 206-244) register an anonymous HttpServlet that re-implements NaruServeServlet.service (adapter.handler(), new ServletExchange(..), afterHandler) so they can keep the exchange. It skips adapter.enter()/leave() and the ServletPath prefix logic, so a change in NaruServeServlet's sequence leaves these tests green while the real path differs; the same 12 lines are duplicated in two files. Also exchanges.poll(5, SECONDS) (SseLimitTest:181, SseAsyncTest:232-233) is dereferenced without a null check, so a missing exchange surfaces as NullPointerException instead of a clear failure; in SseLimitTest the right exchange is selected only because the stream request happens to be the first one queued (the 503 request queues a second one that is then discarded with clear()).
findings.suggested_fix: Capture the exchange from the real NaruServeServlet (for example a package-private hook or a recording subclass of NaruServeServlet) and put the shared helper in one place; assertNotNull the polled exchange.

findings.title: sendFile tests do not cover the abort-mid-copy case or the no-read-into-memory part of SDS-AC-10
findings.description: The test named abortStopsSendFileBeforeTheNextChunk calls ex.abort() before sendFile starts, so it only repeats the abort-then-commit check of ServletAbortTest; it never aborts between two chunks. SDS-AC-10 (wave-8-5) also requires copying 'without reading the file into memory', but sdsAc10 ...CopiesExactlyLength only checks that each write is <= 64 KiB, which a full read followed by slicing also satisfies. The java/nio/file check (68-77) scans only ServletExchange.class, so a reference from a nested class or helper would not be seen.
findings.suggested_fix: Abort from the FakeResponse output stream after the first chunk (write hook) and assert the remaining chunks are not written; rename or drop the current test. Scan ServletExchange$*.class as well, or state the narrower claim in the test name.

findings.title: ServletRawTargetTest swallows IOException with a silent retry and sends every target twice
findings.description: reply() catches any IOException and repeats the request once ('shortcut: one retry ... drop it if it never fires'), so a connection reset that Jetty produces for a rejected target is hidden and the test passes on the second attempt; nothing records whether the retry ever fired, so the shortcut can never be dropped. The first loop (98-103) and the verification loop (107-111) send each of the 12 targets again, which makes the second response the one that is compared with servlet.md while the first one only gets a 400/404 range check.
findings.suggested_fix: Collect the status of the first attempt in one loop and assert against servlet.md in the same pass; count retries and fail the test (or log) when one was needed, or remove the retry.

findings.title: Assertions that cannot fail or tell nothing on failure
findings.description: (1) ServletSseAsyncTest:138 asserts after >= 2500 right after Thread.sleep(2500) measured from t0, which is always true. (2) ServletSettingsTest:58 assertSame(ServletAdapter.class, m.getDeclaringClass()) is a tautology after getDeclaredMethod on that class; only the NoSuchMethodException carries the check. (3) ServletRuleTest:51 assertTrue(status == 204) has no message and no expected/actual value. (4) ServletSettingsTest.sdsAc13 (124-129) asserts count("WARN") == 0 without any positive control, so it cannot show that a LAN warning would have been recorded by that logger on this adapter.
findings.suggested_fix: Drop or replace (1) with the heartbeat count assertion that already follows; use assertEquals(204, ...) in (3); for (4) add a control run with bindAddress 0.0.0.0 on the same logger and assert one WARN there.

findings.title: Tests reach into private members of main classes by reflection
findings.description: ServletCodecTest.builderCodec reads RestApp.Builder.codec; ServletConfigurerTest.java:36-38 and ServletLifecycleTest.java:43-45 read RestApp.Builder.adapter; ServletLifecycleTest.java:100-104 reads ShutdownListener.seconds; ServletSseLimitTest.java:83-87 invokes the internal SseClient.cause(). A rename of any of those private members breaks the tests with NoSuchFieldException/NoSuchMethodException although behavior is unchanged, and the Builder fields belong to a module the Servlet module does not own.
findings.suggested_fix: Expose the needed value through a package-private accessor or an existing public/testFixtures API (for example the access-log cause already asserted via the log line), or accept and document the coupling in one helper class.

findings.title: Proxy-based fakes silently return defaults for unexpected calls
findings.description: ServletWebSocketTest builds HttpServletRequest and WebSocketEndpoint proxies that return null for every method, and ServletAbortTest.FakeResponse (used also by ServletSendFileTest) returns null/false/0 for any call not recorded as an expectation. A primitive-returning call on the request would throw NullPointerException from the proxy rather than report an unexpected call, and a response method the adapter should not call is only caught where a test inspects res.calls. This is inconsistent with ServletAbortTest.request(), which throws AssertionError on any call, and is mock-style stubbing in place of the Jetty request/response available in the module.
findings.suggested_fix: Use the strict ServletAbortTest.request() for the WebSocket exchange and make FakeResponse throw AssertionError for methods outside an explicit allow-list (setStatus, setHeader, addHeader, flushBuffer, getOutputStream, isCommitted).

findings.title: slow() swallows exceptions on the claim that the reply assertion reports them, but one caller never asserts the reply
findings.description: The catch block comment says 'the assertion on the reply reports it'. That is true for sdsAc1 ...refusesAtOnce (127-128) but not for sdsAc1 ...stopReturnsByTheDeadlinePlusOneSecond (133-146): its slow() reply reference is dropped (line 136), so a failed or reset slow request is never reported and the 'slow request is not interrupted' check at 143 rests only on thread liveness.
findings.suggested_fix: Keep the AtomicReference in the second test and assert after proceed.countDown() that the slow reply is 200 'done' (or record the swallowed exception and fail on it).
